 Live updates: Sixers kick off NBA Cup play at home against the Knicks 
 Follow along for live updates as the Sixers host the Knicks in their NBA Cup opener. 
 By Karli Cauley • 
 Published 3 hours ago • 
 Updated 6 seconds ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) during the fourth quarter against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images
 What to Know
 The Sixers enter at 4-1, while the Knicks are 2-3.
 Jaylen Brown was downgraded to out with left knee tendinopathy.
 Jose Alvarado is out with a left ankle sprain. Karl-Anthony Towns will play after being listed as probable with a left wrist sprain.
 Philadelphia beat New York 106-100 in the season opener behind Tyrese Maxey’s 28 points.
 The Sixers overcame a 13-point deficit entering the fourth quarter to beat Indiana on Wednesday.
 Jalen Brunson had 38 points and seven assists in Wednesday’s win over Chicago.
 The Knicks begin their NBA Cup title defense riding a two-game winning streak.
 Tip off is set to begin at 7:30 p.m. ET on Prime.

 Brown out with left knee injury for Sixers vs. Knicks 
 The Sixers downgraded Jaylen Brown’s status to out Friday night before their NBA Cup game vs. the Knicks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
 Initially listed as questionable, Brown was ruled out approximately two hours ahead of tip-off. The official designation for Brown’s injury was “left (knee) patellar tendinopathy.” 
 The other Sixers sidelined by injury were Dominick Barlow, Jabari Walker, Ariel Hukporti and Tacko Fall. Friday’s game is the first of a back-to-back set; the Sixers will hit the road and play the Hornets on Saturday. 
 Brown had a 20-point, 10-rebound night Wednesday in the Sixers’ win over the Pacers. 
 “He reported soreness after the game in Indy,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame Friday. “He wasn’t able to go through shootaround today and was ruled out.”
 Nurse was asked about Brown and Walker each having the same “left patellar tendinopathy” listing. 
 “I think it’s certainly different for each of them,” he said. “I think it’s a timetable of treatment, pain management and getting them feeling better. Hopefully, they’ll both be back soon.”
 Brown’s durability and reliability were significant aspects tha t drew the Sixers to trade for him in the summer. The 30-year-old forward played 71 games last year in an All-NBA season and averaged 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists in 34.4 minutes per contest. 
 Nurse indicated Dean Wade would likely step into Brown’s starting lineup spot.
 “I think we probably are going to do something like start Dean in place of him,” he said, “just because it feels like that will be better matchups once the subs start coming. We’ll be in a better flow for that.”
